Moreover, H.R. 2516 is the second proposal considered by this Committee to weaken the accreditation process specifically for religious institutions. H.R. 4054, the Accreditation Choice and Innovation Act, reported by the Committee at the same time as H.R. 2516, proposed a sweeping exemption allowing religious institutions to skirt accreditation standards for core curricula requirements when those standards were not consistent with the institution's religious mission.\39\
\39\The College Cost Reduction Act, H.R. 6951, 118th Cong. (as reported by the Committee on Education and the Workforce, January 31, 2024).
Taken together, these legislative proposals could undermine the accreditation process and potentially mislead students that their chosen program of study meets the stated accreditation standards without exception. As a result, students may not be aware if they are not being instructed in the core curriculum for their chosen program of study.
It is unclear what problem these accreditation proposals are seeking to solve with respect to the accreditation of religious institutions. The provisions in H.R. 2516 are a solution in search of a problem. Moreover, institutions of higher education remain in a position to choose accreditors that fit their needs. For instance, a college whose curriculum rejects evolution can choose a religious based accreditor.\39\ Current law provides adequate safeguards for religious institutions without potentially undermining the important role of accreditors.
DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING MARKUP OF H.R. 2516
Committee Democrats offered no amendments to H.R. 2516.
CONCLUSION
If enacted into law, H.R. 2516 will do nothing to improve the quality of higher education in America, and all serious analysis suggests the result will be exactly the opposite. For this and the reasons stated above, Committee Democrats unanimously opposed H.R. 2516 when the Committee on Education and the Workforce considered it on June 25, 2025. We strongly urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Suzanne Bonamici,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Summer L. Lee,
Members of Congress.
